questions.q: Which tool does this lesson use to load Accounts, Contacts, and Leads?
options: Data Loader
The Data Import Wizard
The Apex Data API directly
Manual entry only
questions.explain: The Import Wizard is used for Accounts, Contacts, and Leads -- point-and-click with built-in duplicate matching, suited to a few hundred rows.

questions.q: Why does this lesson use Data Loader rather than the Import Wizard for Installation Projects and Service Contracts?
options: The Import Wizard cannot create records at all
Data Loader supports custom objects and multiple related lookups per row, and handles bulk CSV loads the Wizard isn't built for
Installation Projects don't support any lookup fields
Data Loader is required for every object with a picklist field
questions.explain: Data Loader is chosen for its bulk insert/upsert capability and support for custom objects with multiple lookup relationships per row.

questions.q: What is the correct load order for Cascade's sample data, and why?
options: Any order works since Salesforce resolves lookups automatically
Service Contracts first, since they're the most important business data
Accounts, then Contacts, then Opportunities, then Installation Projects, then Service Contracts -- each step's lookups depend on the one before it already existing
Opportunities first, since every other object eventually relates back to a deal
questions.explain: Because later objects look up to earlier ones (Opportunity to Account, Installation Project to Opportunity and Account, Service Contract to Account and Installation Project), loading out of order causes lookup fields to fail to resolve.

questions.q: What does an Upsert operation do that a plain Insert does not?
options: It deletes any record not included in the current load
It updates an existing record that matches on a key field instead of creating a duplicate
It skips all validation rules during the load
It automatically creates Record Types for new picklist values
questions.explain: Upsert matches incoming rows against existing records (via an External ID or similar key) and updates them, rather than inserting a duplicate every time the load runs.

questions.q: Why does this lesson insist on real-sounding business names like "Riverside Bistro Group" instead of "Test Account 1"?
options: Salesforce rejects any Account name containing the word "Test"
Realistic sample data is what actually proves the build works and is presentable in an interview or portfolio, unlike obvious placeholder data
Record Types require a specific naming convention
It's required for the Data Import Wizard to function
questions.explain: The lesson frames this as a portfolio-readiness issue, directly tied to Requirement 9 from Lesson 1's Definition of Done: clean, realistic sample data, not placeholder junk.
